results.title: Softr is rated "Excellent" with 4.3 / 5 on Trustpilot
results.content:
The frustrating part is that Softr has enormous potential. The visual builder is intuitive, development is fast, and when everything works it’s genuinely enjoyable to build with. But a no-code platform aimed at businesses has to be judged on reliability and support, not just how easy it is to create an application.  
  
Softr is not an inexpensive service, and the level of support and platform reliability falls well short of what the pricing suggests. When you’re paying a premium for software that powers client-facing applications, you expect dependable infrastructure, transparent usage management, and responsive support when something goes wrong. In my experience, Softr delivers none of those consistently. [...] What makes this especially frustrating is that there is often nothing you can do to recover the service yourself. You can’t restart failed workflows, manually restore functionality, or access meaningful live support when the platform itself is experiencing problems. Instead, you’re left waiting while your clients are unable to use the systems you’ve built for them.  
  
I’ve also experienced inconsistent platform behaviour, where functionality that previously worked suddenly stops without warning. Hours are then spent trying to determine whether the problem lies in your own application before discovering it’s another platform issue. That uncertainty destroys confidence in the product. [...] The two biggest issues are Softr’s customer support and its credit usage system. Credit consumption is extremely difficult to monitor or manage, and there is no straightforward way to increase capacity when you’re approaching your limit. To make matters worse, the notification system is unreliable—I have experienced outages without receiving any usage warnings that had previously been sent. When this happens, entire workflows are taken offline without warning. Clients are unable to use the system, business operations come to a halt, and you’re left explaining the outage with little or no information from Softr because timely support simply isn’t available.

results.title: Softr - we don’t just want apps, we want systems that actually run businesses - Ask the community - Softr Community
results.content:
The whole AI is not for me but this is not the subject.

There are some super interesting things with the vibe coding block, I create things that I couldn’t do before and for that thank you to the whole Softr team!

On the other hand, it creates frustration, because stability is not always there: editable elements in the settings can disappear partly when I modify the code… I have to make a request again in the chatbot but it costs credits..

The redesign of static blocks is a good thing! Clearly! but also frustrating!!

The ‘Style’ tab has disappeared, as a result, we can no longer manually change the padding for example.

it is necessary to go through the chatbot.. so by using AI credit.. [...] :woman_shrugging:

A timeline of requested updates would be fantastic. If we know it’s not going to be looked at for a while then we can find a workaround and at least set our clients expectations. When we promise them it’s coming soon (because we’ve been told it’s coming soon) it reflects badly on us as business and that’s really frustrating. [...] In the other hand Supabase is a huge step-up from both Airtable and Softr DB; data validation, RLS, SQL functions, Edge (JS) functions, Auth, storage, realtime, etc. You’ll need some basics on SQL to kick-off, but if you are committed, you’ll learn quickly, plus, you can self host and have this monster that can manage thousands of users with practically no limits for records, api calls, none of that, for free.

Your 100% right. AI is not all thing to all people. I use softr to run my business and it has enabled me to reduce admin staff by 8. That’s a big saving. But I have noticed quite a lot of frustrations creeping in for all the reasons you outline.

I agree with most things, if not everything in this thread. I think we can all agree we are at a turning point with technology.

results.title: A new era: build real business software with AI, starting today - Announcements - Softr Community
results.content:
Lack of roadmap visibility + delayed features is creating frustration  
→ users are asking for things for 1–2+ years without clarity on priority or timing

Many of us are not trying to build more apps  
→ we’re trying to build one system that runs our business

I think the core tension is this:

Softr is doing an incredible job at helping people build apps fast  
But the next phase for many of us is needing Softr to help us run businesses reliably

From my side (and echoed by others here): Softr - we don’t just want apps, we want systems that actually run businesses - Ask the community - Softr Community

We’re not asking for everything at once -  
But we are asking for:

Clear prioritisation of core business functionality

Less reliance on AI for things that should be native [...] :rocket:

Agree and we also need full audit log capability so we can properly track who is changing what and when with options restore/revert when required.

Was excited to see what the new release was but disappointed that it’s more AI and not improvements to basic functionality and native blocks that we’ve been waiting months/years on.

A lot of existing Softr users have already spent a significant amount of time building existing apps and we’re waiting on key improvements. We don’t want to be building from scratch using AI which defeats the reason we started using Softr in the first place.

Sorry for the rant. Just getting frustrated with being promised things and then not being delivered :frowning:

:frowning: [...] Less reliance on AI for things that should be native

More visibility into what’s actually being worked on

Confidence that Softr can scale with us as our systems grow

We all want Softr to win - that’s why we’re pushing on this.

Because a lot of us are deeply invested in what we’ve built here.

If Softr can nail this next phase (depth, reliability, core features),  
it becomes incredibly hard to leave.

Look forward to your feedback

results.title: Softr Review: Pros, Cons & a Better Alternative for 2026
results.content:
What really frustrated me was how rigid the design is. The pre-built blocks look clean, but they're so tightly defined that meaningful customization is hard. That lines up with what many reviewers mention about Softr's limited flexibility.

## Is Softr right for you?

Softr is a great fit if you want a quick, no-code way to stand up simple, data-driven portals and internal tools, but it's not ideal for complex apps.

### Who will love it: [...] ### Cons

 Limited customization and design flexibility: Because Softr is block-based, you're somewhat constrained by the layouts and styles it offers. You can tweak things, but you can't fully customize every detail of the design.
 Pricing issues: Softr's pricing plans gate some integrations behind higher tiers. For example, connecting to SQL requires the Business plan, and custom code and API calls require Pro or higher.

## My personal take on Softr

To test Softr, I built a client portal for sharing legal documents. I had the option to build from scratch in the visual builder, use a template, or generate with AI. I chose AI. [...] Incredibly easy to learn: Users consistently call Softr one of the simplest no-code platforms available. One reviewer on G2 likes how "easy to use, transfer data into it, and navigate the interface."
 Airtable integration: Users love that they can spin up branded interfaces on top of Airtable data. They don't have to use the native Interfaces which have limited features. Airtable remains the backend where all the data lives, and Softr becomes the layer users interact with.
 Customer support is responsive: Multiple reviewers highlighted the support team. The founders are also active in online communities and respond directly to feedback.
